evidence:
SOURCES READ: frozen workbook rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx read in memory via zipfile (Quality Checks row 41 = check 40 'The rubric produces a spread across partial-quality apps, not all-or-nothing.'; Internal Quality Checks row 41 has no annotation for check 40; row 42's internal note says scoring practice is binary + weighted); skill SKILL.md (Likert-vs-weighted known false positive; reward shaped 0.6/0.2/0.2 behind zero-weight gates and a functional floor) and references/quality-checks.md section '40 · reward_is_graded_not_binary_and_discriminates' ('A single all-or-nothing gate, or criteria that all depend on one precondition, collapses the signal'); qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (pipeline requires a hash-bound runtime record for reward discrimination before local clearance); frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template (tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py and tests/test.sh are byte-identical to the task's: diff -q reports no difference); handoffs/LESSONS_FROM_COLDERWATER_2026-10-08.md (lessons 2, 3, 4, 5 bear on this row).

STRUCTURE (supports a graded reward): tests/scoring.toml:1-11 gates render/constraints 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05; tests/tools/score.py:40-48 reward = weighted mean if gates passed and functional > 0.05, else 0. Each gate is one binary criterion (gates/render/judge.toml hro_gate_render: wrong password refused + Recruiter sign-in shows a usable workspace; gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared: add one candidate, reload, Observer reads it in an independent context). These are simple load/reload/server-backed gates per lesson 4, with permissions and workspace rules explicitly left to scored outcomes. Scored suite: functional has 15 binary criteria in mode='individual' (scored/functional/judge.toml:3; aggregation weighted_mean :21; weights 4.5,4,3,4,5.5,5,5,2,4,4.5,4,2,5.5,3.5,4.5 = 61, documented as 1.0/1.5/2.0 per leg at :23-25, consistent with lesson 2); polish has 5 binary (weights 2,2,2,1.5,2 = 9.5, weighted_mean); visual has 5 likert points=5 with five described anchors each, raw 1 normalizing to 0 (scored/visual/prompt.md:12,20), so 21 possible visual levels. Precondition decoupling is explicit: scored/functional/prompt.md:21 'Where your criterion needs a job and no job can be opened through the UI (opening is graded only in hro_intake_restart), use the seeded Product Designer job...' plus the setup-dependency rule (judge against the state the app produced, or leave a pure setup leg out); hro_undo, hro_activity, hro_readonly_roles, hro_messaging, hro_unread_seen and the hro_pol_* rows carry explicit leg-removal or fallback wording for features graded elsewhere; functional prompt :9-11,17 and polish prompt :12 say one criterion per session / continue after a failed leg. So no single precondition collapses all criteria: an app that cannot open jobs can still earn rows via the seeded job and seeded conversations, and an app without live updates still earns the non-live rows (moves, reject_reopen, bulk, undo, roles, intake, drafts). Worked arithmetic from the shipped policy: passing only hro_drafts + hro_activity gives F = 4/61 = 0.066 > floor and reward = 0.6*0.066 + 0.2*P + 0.2*V = 0.039 + 0.2V (+0.2P), V in steps of 0.05; the reachable reward set is many-valued, not {0,1}.

RISKS (unresolved): (1) Coarse conjunctive units. Every functional criterion ends 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold' over many legs (e.g. hro_intake_restart :33 has ~15 legs incl. case-insensitive duplicate email, refusal shown at the email field with the form retained, places 2.5, recruiter-as-manager replay, restart without reseed; hro_interview_places :69 requires focus on a control of the refused card; hro_two_people :60 requires 409 and naming the changer). The 61 'leg weights' only size each criterion and never give partial credit, so the reward moves in 15 functional + 5 polish binary steps. Lesson 3 says the target builder's weaknesses are edge cases inside core features, and most rows here bundle a core flow with at least one such edge. An app with every core flow working but one distinct edge miss in most rows scores near F = 0 like a much weaker app, and if F <= 0.05 (under ~3.05 of 61 weight passed) score.py:47-48 zeros the reward despite good polish/visual. Whether this compresses realistic partial apps to 0 is an empirical question that source reading cannot settle. (2) Required measurement missing: qc/runs/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r6/raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; its only entries are the scripted golden driver (26 groups PASS, via-solve.log), which is not a judge run and says nothing about spread across weak or partial apps. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a hash-bound reward-discrimination record before clearance; none exists, and a Note cannot waive it. (3) The in-dimension gate repeats in all 15 functional sessions plus polish and visual; judge noise there zeros a whole unit (another all-or-nothing source per criterion), unmeasured.

LESSONS CHECK: lesson 4 (simple gates) satisfied, both gates are single simple binary checks; lesson 2 (one documented weight scheme) satisfied; lessons 3/5 (land in 0.1-0.7): the brief carries the self-check line (instruction.md:13 'Before you hand it over, please check it yourself the way we'll use it...'), but no model or Oracle run exists for this candidate, so band placement is unmeasured; lesson 21: no rerun claims made here.

ADVERSARIAL: Broken app that could score high: a static or seed-copy app fails both gates (independent-context readback of a newly added card), so reward 0; no inflated spread found. Conforming partial app that could be under-scored: one implementing every core flow but missing the changer name in 409 refusals, the post-refusal focus target, case-insensitive duplicate email, the reason restore on undoing a reopening and the 'sending counts as reading' unread rule loses hro_two_people, hro_interview_places, hro_intake_restart, hro_reject_reopen and hro_long_thread (22 of 61) for five small misses; still a spread (F about 0.64), so not a demonstrated collapse. A collapse needs one miss in nearly every row; plausible for the target builder but unmeasured.

counterexample: Hypothetical, unmeasured: an app whose core board, messaging and role flows all work but which misses one distinct edge leg in most functional rows (no changer name in the 409, wrong focus after a capacity refusal, case-sensitive duplicate email, undo not detecting a colleague's re-order, sending not clearing unread, and so on) can pass under ~3.05/61 functional weight, hit the 0.05 functional floor and score 0, the same as a far weaker app, even with good polish and visual.
suggested_fix: Produce the missing reward-discrimination record by scoring a few mutated weak/partial apps with the configured judge; if partial apps collapse to 0, split the heaviest bundles so core flows and their edge legs earn credit separately, without changing scoring.toml or score.py.
